title: The Shadow
paragraphs: A crime and mystery series featuring the mysterious Shadow, most famously Lamont Cranston, who uses secrecy, disguise, and the ability to cloud men's minds while battling criminals and protecting the innocent.
Crime/mystery drama built around Lamont Cranston as The Shadow and companion Margo Lane. The dramatic series began September 26, 1937 after earlier radio use of The Shadow as a mysterious narrator.

The run breaks into several distinct periods: Orson Welles lead era (September 26, 1937 to September 18, 1938) on [[org|org.09b709d4bde5c263|Mutual Broadcasting System]], Bill Johnstone lead era (September 25, 1938 to March 21, 1943) on [[org|org.09b709d4bde5c263|Mutual Broadcasting System]], Bret Morrison first lead era (September 26, 1943 to June 30, 1944) on [[org|org.09b709d4bde5c263|Mutual Broadcasting System]], and John Archer lead era (September 1, 1944 to June 30, 1945) on [[org|org.09b709d4bde5c263|Mutual Broadcasting System]].

Names that turn up again and again in the surviving run include Elsie Thompson (organist), Ken Roberts (announcer and performer), William Johnstone (performer), [[person|bret-morrison|Bret Morrison]] (performer), Marjorie Anderson (performer), John Cole (director and producer), and Paul Huber (commercial spokesman and performer).
Across its run, the surviving broadcasts are tied to [[org|org.09b709d4bde5c263|Mutual Broadcasting System]], [[org|org.666407112636e085|Michelson]], and [[org|org.50630574777d6937|Don Lee Network]].

The stories often return to murder and violent crime, supernatural and occult threats, secret identity and disguise, gangs and organized crime, prisons, execution and criminal justice, and mad science and dangerous inventions.
The show also sits in a wider radio history that includes The Shadow across radio and pulp publishing, Sponsored radio crime drama and premium culture, and Wartime espionage and sabotage themes.

If you are following the same actors and creative circles, related programs worth opening next include [[show|columbia-workshop|Columbia Workshop]], [[show|words-at-war|Words at War]], [[show|x-minus-one|X Minus One]], [[show|cbs-radio-mystery-theater|CBS Radio Mystery Theater]], and [[show|the-chase|The Chase]].
